milestone.title: mp-handoff — two-round review hand-off protocol between coordinator and runner

intent.outcome: After this ships, the `mp-handoff` skill is the cross-cutting hand-off protocol that defines what data passes, what session-boundary discipline applies, and what evidence the runner leaves for the coordinator (and vice versa) at each stage transition in the 12-stage mp-flow timeline. M123 closes the L5 lesson ("same-session self-review is unreliable") at the protocol level: the runner session that produces code (stages 5-7) is not the same session that fixes the coordinator's findings (stage 9); the coordinator's review session (stages 8 + 10) is not the same session that did the planning (stages 1-4). The protocol covers four hand-off points across the 12-stage timeline. The protocol is documented in `templates/skills/mp-handoff/SKILL.md` and tested end-to-end.

problem.description: The two-round review pattern (runner self-reviews, coordinator externally reviews) is the L5 lesson applied to the mp workflow. M120 surfaces the role-binding at a high level; M121 owns the coordinator's reviewing sub-mode; M122 owns the runner's fixing sub-mode. None of these is the protocol — the explicit 'what data passes, what session-boundary, what evidence' content. Without M123, the hand-off discipline is documented three times in different files (M120, M121, M122) with slightly different framings, and the integration test for the full hand-off is missing. A dedicated M123 makes the hand-off protocol first-class, single-source, and integration-tested.

in_scope: `templates/skills/mp-handoff/SKILL.md` (the hand-off protocol) — the canonical reference for what data passes at each of the FOUR hand-off points in the 12-stage mp-flow timeline, what session-boundary applies, what evidence the producing side leaves for the consuming side. The four points are: (a) coordinator → runner at stage 4 → 5 (Approve → Claim & execute; the mp-flow entry); (b) runner → coordinator at stage 7 → 8 (Complete → External review; round-1 hand-off with self-review findings as data); (c) coordinator → runner at stage 8 → 9 (External review with findings → Remediate; round-2 hand-off with external findings as data); (d) runner → coordinator at stage 9 → 10 (Remediate → Re-review; the loop-back hand-off).

Stage-transition contracts: per transition, the protocol names the data (findings, evidence, lifecycle state, blockers, spec context), the session-boundary (which side's session id closes — never the same session across the boundary per L5), and the evidence (the audit trail the producing side leaves).

Session-boundary discipline: the L5 lesson applied to the mp workflow. The runner session that produces code (stages 5-7) is not the same session that fixes the coordinator's findings (stage 9). The coordinator's review session (stages 8 + 10) is not the same session that did the planning (stages 1-4). M123 is the protocol-level enforcement; the SKILL.md files in M120/M121/M122 cross-link.

Integration test: a session walks the full cycle including the (a) planner→runner hand-off at stage 4→5 plus the round-1/2 review loop (stages 7→8→9→10). The test asserts session ids differ between rounds (session-boundary rule). The (a) hand-off is the mp-flow entry — the test verifies that a fresh runner session receives the approved spec + planning notes and proceeds.

`mp install --skills=mp-handoff` deploys the protocol skill. mp-flow (M120) cross-references it from the stage-transition section; mp-coordinator (M121) and mp-runner (M122) reference it in their hand-off contract sections.
out_of_scope: The L5 lesson content itself — it ships in `docs/code-review-lessons.md`; M123 surfaces the lesson at a protocol level only.
The cross-role flow timeline (M120) — M123 is the protocol; the 12-stage timeline is in M120.
The role-specific deep-dives (M121, M122) — M123 is the hand-off between them; the roles themselves live in M121 and M122.
The runnable Pattern: blocks for L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 (M99 archival gap) — M123 references the lessons doc; the runnable patterns are a deferred work item.

The hand-off implementation (code that does the data exchange) — the protocol is documented; the code that wires it is the harness's concern, not mp's. M123 verifies that the SKILL.md files cross-reference the protocol (content-completeness test), not that the harness enforces the session boundary at runtime (harness-level test).

Each point names (1) the data, (2) the session-boundary (which side's session id closes — never the same session across the boundary per L5), (3) the evidence the producing side leaves.

design_decisions.choice: Three hand-off points (runner→coordinator, coordinator→runner with findings, runner→coordinator after fixing). Documented as three subsections in SKILL.md. Each is a distinct data + session-boundary + evidence shape. Folding them into one would obscure the per-transition differences (the first and third are runner→coordinator but with different data).
design_decisions.rationale: Three hand-off points have three distinct contracts. The protocol names all three explicitly. A future addition (e.g., a fourth hand-off from planner→executor in a brownfield) is straightforward — add a fourth subsection to SKILL.md.

design_decisions.area: Why a separate `mp-handoff` skill instead of folding the protocol into `mp-flow`:
design_decisions.choice: M120 is the cross-role timeline; M123 is the hand-off protocol between roles. The timeline says 'stage 2 hands off to stage 3'; the protocol says 'here's what data, here's the session-boundary, here's the evidence.' Different content. A separate skill lets the harness load mp-handoff when the agent enters a hand-off state (mid-`mp milestone complete`, for example), independent of the timeline.
design_decisions.rationale: Single source of truth for the protocol. The L5 enforcement lives in the protocol skill, not in the timeline skill; the timeline cross-links to it.

design_decisions.area: Hand-off point (a) data includes AC verification integrity report
design_decisions.choice: Hand-off point (a) Approve -> Claim & execute (M123 AC-01 a) data is extended with a verification integrity report: a per-AC table resolving each AC's verification command. The producer (coordinator, stage 4 Approve) runs the M121 integrity pre-flight (mp plan verify-ac <id>) and emits the report as part of the hand-off payload. The consumer (runner, stage 5 Claim & execute) rejects the hand-off when any AC verification is unresolvable.
design_decisions.rationale: Defense in depth for the AC verification integrity contract (M120 F-01 and F-02 follow-up, M121 design_decision). M121 catches bogus verifications at review time; M123 enforces it at the hand-off boundary so the runner never accepts a milestone with unresolvable verifications even if the review-time check was bypassed. The runner does NOT silently fix bad verifications - that is a spec defect, not a runner defect; the hand-off rejects and surfaces the report rows.

findings.description: AC-04 verification was originally "cargo test -p raul --lib mp_handoff_content_completeness" but the test actually lives in -p mp and is named handoff_protocol_session_boundary_enforced. Fixed during execution: amended AC-04 verification to point at the actual test assertion. Same class as M120 F-01/F-02, M122 F-05 — AC verification strings drift from where tests actually live. The reviewer-time defense (M121 AC-09 verify-ac) would catch this if the verification referenced a real test target; updating the verification after the fact is reactive. Lesson: when writing AC verifications, point at test paths that will exist after the step executes, not aspirational paths.

findings.description: AC-04 description claims 'a session walks the full cycle ... The test asserts session ids differ between rounds (session-boundary rule)' but the actual test (handoff_protocol_session_boundary_enforced) is content-completeness only — it asserts SKILL.md keyword presence, not runtime session-id differences. F-01 amended the verification string to point at the right test, but the description still reads aspirational. Future agents will look for a session-walk test that doesn't exist. Fix: amend the description to content-completeness scope; the session-id runtime check is the harness's concern, out of scope for mp (matches AC-04's own parenthetical).

findings.description: Step S3 tests field (master-plan/milestones/123-...json:185) is a broken shell command: 'for handoff in ...; do grep -A5 "" templates/skills/mp-handoff/SKILL.md | grep -q "data:" && ...; done'. 'grep -A5 ""' has no pattern, errors with exit 2; the for-loop body's first command always errors, && short-circuits, and the loop never reaches the other grep -q checks. The loop variable $handoff is unused. This is the 1 step-test force-bypassed in the verification evidence. The actual content check is correctly done by handoff_skill_three_section_contract in the Rust integration test. Fix: replace S3.tests with 'cargo test -p mp --test handoff_protocol_session_boundary_enforced handoff_skill_three_section_contract' — matches AC-03's verification string and is consistent with the M117 step-test discipline.

findings.description: crates/mp/tests/handoff_protocol_session_boundary_enforced.rs:48-61 — handoff_skill_three_section_contract asserts each of 'Data', 'Session-boundary', 'Evidence' appears >= 4 times anywhere in SKILL.md. The '## Session-boundary discipline (L5)' heading and the closing 'Stage-transition contract' block each contain the words but are not hand-off-point tables. A SKILL.md that moved all 4 occurrences into the L5 section and emptied the four hand-off tables would still pass. The assertion over-counts. Fix: tighten to per-section assertions — split SKILL.md on the four '^## Hand-off point' blocks and assert each block has Data/Session-boundary/Evidence rows.
